newSection.name: JL

newSection.name: Jimaku

newSection.name: ッツ Ebook Reader

newSection.name: asbplayer

newSection.name: owocr

newSection.name: Lute v3

newSection.name: Memento

newSection.name: Mokuro

newSection.name: exSTATic

bundles.title: Flashcards & SRS
bundles.blurb: Spaced repetition — the backbone of vocab retention. Pick one and stick with it.

items.name: Anki
items.description: The free, open-source SRS almost every immersion learner uses. Desktop + AnkiWeb sync; AnkiMobile (paid) on iOS.

items.name: AnkiWeb
items.description: Free cloud sync + browser review for your Anki decks across devices.

items.name: FSRS
items.description: Modern scheduling algorithm built into recent Anki — fewer reviews for the same retention. Turn it on in deck options.

items.name: jpdb
items.description: Japanese-specific SRS with prebuilt decks mined from real books, anime, and VNs. Great for reading-first learners.

items.name: Kitsun
items.description: Polished web SRS with community decks and reading/listening modes. A friendlier paid alternative to Anki.

checklist.text: Install Anki on desktop and make a free AnkiWeb account to sync.
Download a starter vocab deck (Kaishi 1.5k is the current recommended beginner deck).
Enable FSRS in deck options for a lighter, smarter review schedule.
Do your reviews every single day — consistency beats volume.
Once comfortable, start adding your own words mined from things you read.

bundles.title: Kanji & writing
bundles.blurb: Learn to recognize and write kanji. Recognition matters most for reading — pick a method and be consistent.

items.name: WaniKani
items.description: Radical → kanji → vocabulary SRS with mnemonics. Structured and beginner-friendly; free for the first 3 levels.

items.name: Kanji Study (Android)
items.description: Deep, offline Android app for kanji recognition and stroke-order writing practice.

items.name: Remembering the Kanji (RTK)
items.description: Heisig's classic method for memorizing kanji meanings and writing via stories. Pair with the Kanji Koohii community.

items.name: Kanji Koohii
items.description: Free companion to RTK — shared mnemonic stories and built-in SRS for the kanji.

items.name: Ringotan
items.description: Free SRS app focused purely on handwriting kanji from memory, ordered to match RTK/WaniKani/textbooks.

checklist.text: Pick ONE kanji method (WaniKani, RTK, or KanjiStudy) — do not run several at once.
Learn the common radicals first; they make every later kanji easier.
Prioritize recognition (kanji → meaning/reading) over handwriting if your goal is reading.
Add handwriting with Ringotan only if you specifically want to write by hand.

bundles.title: Grammar
bundles.blurb: Grammar guides and references. Read through one guide once, then use the rest as look-up references.

items.name: Tae Kim — Guide to Japanese
items.description: The classic free beginner grammar guide. Clear, structured, and enough to start reading with a dictionary.

items.name: Bunpro
items.description: Grammar SRS that drills points in context with links out to explanations. Structured JLPT paths.

items.name: Cure Dolly — Organic Japanese
items.description: YouTube series explaining Japanese grammar structurally (the “invisible が”). Odd voice, excellent mental model.

items.name: Imabi
items.description: Extremely thorough free grammar reference, from beginner to very advanced. Dense — best as a reference.

items.name: Sakubi
items.description: A concise, fast, free grammar guide designed to get you to immersion quickly.

items.name: Dictionary of Japanese Grammar (DoJG)
items.description: The Basic/Intermediate/Advanced reference set — the gold-standard grammar dictionary. Also on Yomitan.

checklist.text: Read one full beginner grammar guide (Tae Kim or Sakubi) — do not memorize, just absorb.
Make sure you can read hiragana and katakana before starting grammar.
Keep a reference (Imabi or DoJG) open to look up points as you meet them in reading.
Reinforce grammar by seeing it in real sentences, not by drilling rules in isolation.

bundles.title: Listening & audio
bundles.blurb: Train your ears. Start with beginner-friendly podcasts and build up to native content.

items.name: Nihongo con Teppei (Beginner)
items.description: Short, all-Japanese beginner podcast episodes. Perfect first listening resource — hundreds of free episodes.

items.name: Comprehensible Japanese
items.description: Video lessons graded by level using visuals so you understand from day one. Free samples + paid library.

items.name: YouGlish (Japanese)
items.description: Hear any word or phrase pronounced in thousands of real YouTube clips with context.

items.name: asbplayer
items.description: Browser extension for subtitle-synced immersion and mining sentences with audio from video.

items.name: condensed audio (guide)
items.description: Strip the silence out of shows to get dense listening practice on the go. TheMoeWay explains the workflow.

checklist.text: Add a beginner all-Japanese podcast (Nihongo con Teppei) to your phone.
Listen a little every day, even passively — commute, chores, walks.
Prioritize content you mostly understand over content that is too hard.
Gradually mix in native anime/podcasts as your ear adjusts.

bundles.title: Reading & immersion
bundles.blurb: Reading is where it all comes together. Start graded, then move to native material with a pop-up dictionary.

items.name: Tadoku graded readers
items.description: Free level-graded readers for extensive reading. The gentlest on-ramp to reading Japanese.

items.name: NHK News Web Easy
items.description: Real news rewritten in simple Japanese with furigana and audio. Great early native reading.

items.name: ッツ Ebook Reader (ttu)
items.description: Free browser EPUB reader built for Japanese immersion — works beautifully with Yomitan pop-up lookups.

items.name: Mokuro
items.description: Runs OCR over manga so you can hover-look-up words in the text directly. Reads manga in your browser.

items.name: Learn Natively
items.description: Community difficulty grading for Japanese books, manga, and more — find reading at your level.

checklist.text: Start with graded readers (Tadoku) — pick books you can read without stopping much.
Install Yomitan so you can hover over words for instant dictionary lookups.
Read your first easy native thing (NHK Easy or a simple manga) even if it is slow.
Accept ambiguity — you do not need to understand every word to make progress.

bundles.title: Chinese
bundles.blurb: Learning Mandarin too? These are the community favorites for reading-first Chinese.

items.name: Pleco
items.description: The essential Chinese dictionary app. Free core is superb; paid add-ons for OCR, flashcards, and more.

items.name: Hack Chinese
items.description: Spaced-repetition vocab platform built specifically for Chinese learners.

items.name: Du Chinese
items.description: Graded reading app with audio and tap-to-look-up, from absolute beginner up.

items.name: Heavenly Path
items.description: The definitive free guide and reading roadmap for learning to read Chinese through immersion.

items.name: Hanly (grammar)
items.description: Structured Chinese grammar lessons for beginners.

checklist.text: Learn pinyin and the four tones first — get the sounds right early.
Install Pleco as your everyday dictionary.
Follow the Heavenly Path roadmap for what to read and when.
Read graded stories daily (Du Chinese) and look up what you do not know.

bundles.title: Russian
bundles.blurb: A starter set for Russian — alphabet, graded readers, and learner tools.

items.name: Russian With Max
items.description: Comprehensible-input videos and podcast graded for learners, from beginner up.

items.name: Learn Russian (RT alphabet guide)
items.description: Free structured lessons that start from the Cyrillic alphabet and basic grammar.

items.name: Russian LingQ
items.description: Read and listen to graded and native texts with integrated look-up and vocabulary tracking.

items.name: Wiktionary (Russian)
items.description: Free dictionary with full declension/conjugation tables — essential for Russian word forms.

checklist.text: Learn to read the Cyrillic alphabet first — a weekend is enough.
Start comprehensible-input listening (Russian With Max) early.
Get a gentle first look at the case system; do not try to master it up front.
Read graded texts with look-up (LingQ) and let vocab build naturally.

bundles.title: Absolute beginner path
bundles.blurb: Brand new? Do these steps in order. This is the single most-recommended starting route.

items.name: Tofugu — Learn Hiragana
items.description: The best free hiragana guide, with mnemonics. Start here on day one.

items.name: Tofugu — Learn Katakana
items.description: Same mnemonic method for katakana. Do it right after hiragana.

items.name: TheMoeWay — Starter Guide
items.description: A complete, free, step-by-step immersion roadmap from zero. The community reference route.

items.name: Refold — Japanese roadmap
items.description: A structured stage-by-stage immersion method with clear milestones.

items.name: r/LearnJapanese Starter Guide
items.description: The subreddit’s consensus getting-started wiki. Good sanity check against hype.

checklist.text: Learn hiragana (about a week).
Learn katakana (about a week).
Start a core vocab SRS deck (Kaishi 1.5k in Anki).
Read a beginner grammar guide (Tae Kim or Sakubi).
Install Yomitan for pop-up dictionary lookups.
Start your first easy immersion (graded readers, simple anime with JP subs).

bundles.title: Output & speaking
bundles.blurb: Ready to produce the language? Practice writing and speaking with real people and get corrected.

items.name: HelloTalk
items.description: Language-exchange app to chat with native speakers by text and voice.

items.name: italki
items.description: Book affordable 1-on-1 lessons or conversation practice with tutors and teachers.

items.name: LangCorrect
items.description: Write journal entries and get free corrections from native speakers.

items.name: VRChat (Japanese worlds)
items.description: Immersive spoken practice with real Japanese speakers in social VR. Popular with immersion learners.

items.name: Shadowing (method guide)
items.description: How to shadow native audio to improve pronunciation and fluency. TheMoeWay’s output guide.

checklist.text: Get a solid base of input first — output is much easier after lots of listening/reading.
Start with low-pressure writing (LangCorrect) and get corrections.
Shadow native audio to train pronunciation and rhythm.
Book a tutor or language exchange when you want real conversation.

bundles.title: Tools & tech
bundles.blurb: The utility belt — pop-up dictionaries, text hookers, and OCR that power an immersion setup.

items.name: Yomitan
items.description: The essential browser pop-up dictionary (successor to Yomichan). Hover any Japanese word for instant lookups + one-click Anki mining.

items.name: Textractor
items.description: Hooks text out of visual novels and games so you can look it up and mine it.

items.name: JL
items.description: Fast Windows pop-up dictionary for reading text from games, VNs, and the clipboard.

items.name: Anki-Connect
items.description: Anki add-on that lets Yomitan and other tools create cards automatically.

items.name: ShareX
items.description: Free screen-capture + OCR tool handy for mining text from images and untextractable games.

checklist.text: Install Yomitan and import a dictionary (JMdict) + a frequency list.
Install Anki-Connect so Yomitan can make cards in one click.
For VNs/games, set up Textractor or JL to capture on-screen text.
Keep an OCR tool (ShareX / owocr) around for anything you cannot hook.
